answer: For a tundra logistics market, every agent must reserve a route slot and place a bond before a buyer reveals random delivery checkpoints between an oasis and the depot. A signed checkpoint receipt can be redeemed once, so hollow aliases cannot multiply payment from one trip. To operate ten identities, an attacker needs ten vehicles, crews, deposits and simultaneous radio links; missed checkpoints burn the bond. A wealthy operator can still hire capacity, and colluding drivers may fake receipts, so inspectors sample routes and cross-check fuel and location records.
